\[
n(r_0) = \sum_{\lvert r - r_0 \rvert \le 3.4} e^{-\left(\frac{I(r) - I(r_0)}{t}\right)^6},
\qquad
R(r_0) = \begin{cases} g - n(r_0) & n(r_0) < g \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},
\qquad
t = 25,\ g = 0.5 \cdot 37
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(r_0\): The nucleus, the center pixel
- \(n\): The USAN area, from 0 to 37
- \(t\): The brightness threshold
- \(g\): The geometric threshold

Around each pixel, the nucleus r_0, a disk of 37 pixels is placed. Each pixel in it counts as similar to the nucleus by a smooth step. It is about 1 when their brightness differs by much less than t, and about 0 when it differs by much more. The sum n is the USAN area, the univalue segment assimilating nucleus. In a flat area all 37 pixels are similar. On a straight edge about half are. At a corner, fewer are, the fewer the sharper the corner. So the response R grows as n falls below the geometric threshold g. Corners are the pixels where R is above 0 and the largest in its 5 x 5 neighborhood.
